answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works through a stake-and-reputation bridge: each agent posts a bond slashable if its attestations are contradicted, released only after a long challenge window. A swarm of fake identities cannot form cheaply because every member must lock real capital, and the cipher binding each key to its on-chain history makes copied reputation traceable. The inlet for newcomers stays open, but the attacker pays N times the bond and forfeits it once peers flag the cluster.
